Subject: [PATCH] bonding: limit BOND_MODE_8023AD to Ethernet devices

BOND_MODE_8023AD makes sense for ARPHRD_ETHER only.

 lacpdu_mcast_addr+0x0/0x40

Fixes: 872254dd6b1f ("net/bonding: Enable bonding to enslave non ARPHRD_ETHER")
Reported-by: syzbot+9c081b17773615f24672@syzkaller.appspotmail.com
Closes: https://lore.kernel.org/netdev/6966946b.a70a0220.245e30.0002.GAE@google.com/T/#u
Signed-off-by: Eric Dumazet <edumazet@google.com>
Cc: Andrew Lunn <andrew+netdev@lunn.ch>
Acked-by: Jay Vosburgh <jv@jvosburgh.net>

diff --git a/drivers/net/bonding/bond_main.c b/drivers/net/bonding/bond_main.c
index 3d56339a8a10..0aca6c937297 100644
--- a/drivers/net/bonding/bond_main.c
+++ b/drivers/net/bonding/bond_main.c
@@ -1862,6 +1862,12 @@ int bond_enslave(struct net_device *bond_dev, struct net_device *slave_dev,
 	 */
 	if (!bond_has_slaves(bond)) {
 		if (bond_dev->type != slave_dev->type) {
+			if (slave_dev->type != ARPHRD_ETHER &&
+			    BOND_MODE(bond) == BOND_MODE_8023AD) {
+				SLAVE_NL_ERR(bond_dev, slave_dev, extack,
+					     "8023AD mode requires Ethernet devices");
+				return -EINVAL;
+			}
 			slave_dbg(bond_dev, slave_dev, "change device type from %d to %d\n",
 				  bond_dev->type, slave_dev->type);
 
-- 
2.34.1

The patch adds a validation check in the `bond_enslave()` function to prevent enslaving a non-Ethernet device when the bonding mode is `BOND_MODE_8023AD`.  

**Modification in `drivers/net/bonding/bond_main.c`:**  
- Inside the existing block that handles the first slave and detects a device type mismatch between the bond device and the slave device, a new condition is added.  
- If the slave device type is not `ARPHRD_ETHER` and the bond mode is `BOND_MODE_8023AD`, the function returns `-EINVAL` and logs an error message: `"8023AD mode requires Ethernet devices"`.  

**Relationship:**  
- The fix restricts `BOND_MODE_8023AD` (802.3ad link aggregation) to Ethernet devices only, because the 802.3ad implementation relies on Ethernet‑specific multicast addresses (`lacpdu_mcast_addr`). Without this check, enslaving a non‑Ethernet device (e.g., a device with a different header type) leads to an out‑of‑bounds memory access.  
- The change is minimal and precisely addresses the root cause by rejecting the unsupported configuration early, before any attempt to manipulate hardware addresses or multicast lists occurs.
